overview: Morocco is a country in north-west Africa, with coasts on both the Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea. Its capital is Rabat, and its largest city is Casablanca. Morocco is a kingdom and became independent from France and Spain in 1956. Arabic and Berber (Tamazight) are official languages, and cities such as Marrakesh and Fez are famous for their old walled medinas.

geography.text: The Atlas Mountains run across the middle of Morocco, separating the coast from the Sahara Desert in the south-east, and Toubkal in the High Atlas is the highest peak in North Africa. The Rif mountains rise along the Mediterranean coast, and the Atlantic plains are the most fertile part of the country.

history.text: Berber kingdoms ruled the region in ancient times, and Islam arrived in the 600s. Powerful dynasties such as the Almoravids and Almohads ruled from Marrakesh over much of North Africa and Spain. The Alaouite dynasty has ruled since the 1600s. France and Spain divided Morocco in 1912, and it regained independence in 1956.

events.title: Idrisid dynasty
events.text: Idris I founds the first Moroccan Islamic dynasty.

events.title: University of al-Qarawiyyin
events.text: Fatima al-Fihri founds a centre of learning in Fez.

government.text: Morocco is a constitutional monarchy. The King holds significant power over religion, the army and foreign policy, and appoints the Prime Minister from the party that wins most seats in parliament. Morocco controls most of Western Sahara, whose status is disputed.

economy.text: Morocco is the world's largest exporter of phosphates, used in fertiliser. It has become a big car manufacturer and exports fruit, vegetables and textiles. Tourism is major, and Africa's first high-speed railway opened in Morocco in 2018.

culture.text: Morocco's culture mixes Arab, Amazigh (Berber), African and Andalusian influences. Its old cities, such as Marrakesh and Fez, are full of markets called souks. Tagine, couscous and mint tea are famous, and couscous is listed by UNESCO.

items.title: Jemaa el-Fnaa
items.text: Marrakesh's square of storytellers and food stalls.

sport.text: Football is a national passion. In 2022 Morocco became the first African team to reach a World Cup semi-final. It co-hosts the 2030 World Cup with Spain and Portugal and hosted the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations. Runners such as Hicham El Guerrouj have won Olympic golds.

items.text: First African team in a World Cup semi-final.

items.title: Hicham El Guerrouj
items.text: Mile and 1,500 m world record holder.

didYouKnow: The University of al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, founded in 859, is often called the oldest working university in the world.
